notes: Caller evidence proves this owner takes no arguments; the family-assisted m2c draft incorrectly inherited the four-argument signature of its exact template.
The generated u16-pointer increment advanced four bytes per tile. The retained semantic reconstruction corrects it to the two-byte walk emitted by the owner.

A 5,000-candidate safe family-template walk reached 168 bytes and 80 differing halfwords through artificial address-taken scalar temporaries. That generated spelling is not retained as canonical source because it obscures the recovered tile-marking behavior and is still far from exact.
Exact-C adoption remains gated on an independently compiled zero-difference object.

rejected_experiments.experiment: family transfer of the byte-exact template's ascending for-loop idiom (ui/window/clear_tile_attributes_in_rect.c, |= 2 kept, RENDER_ALT_OFS/RENDER_TILE_ATTR_OFS constants confirmed identical for EN)
rejected_experiments.result: worse (100 wrong instructions): the reference retains an explicit width!=0 guard before the row loop (movs r6,#20; cmp r3,#0; beq) that the template's fixed-4-argument for-loop shape does not emit. This owner's fixed 30x20 constant-loop shares only the inner tile-masking logic with the template, not its loop idiom.

rejected_experiments.experiment: hoisting the width!=0 guard to wrap the whole row loop instead of re-testing per iteration
rejected_experiments.result: byte-identical to the un-hoisted do-while-with-inner-check spelling; GCC's own loop-invariant code motion already performs this hoist regardless of source placement. The real ~16-byte/8-instruction gap is not guard placement.

rejected_experiments.experiment: splitting the inner column walk into a static MarkRow(base, cursor, alternate, width) helper taking width as a real function parameter (not a local literal), called twice with the literal 30, on the theory that GCC 2.96 would substitute the constant into the inlined body without re-running dead-branch elimination on it, thereby preserving a runtime width!=0 test the way the reference does
rejected_experiments.result: worse, not better: candidate collapsed to 92 candidate bytes (versus 160 before) at 87 differing halfwords / 93 wrong instructions. The router's inliner still fully constant-propagates through the static helper and eliminates the always-true guard, and the smaller helper body lets it additionally cross-jump/merge more of the surrounding row loop than the flat version did, moving further from the reference shape rather than closer. Confirms the guard-retention gap is a property of the compiler's handling of this exact call/inline shape at the routed optimization level, not something reachable by relocating the same source-level condition.
